title: Variance reduction and disposal of initial moduli
statement: Let f be as in problem.md, d=deg f, and c=ζ(2)^(−1), where ζ is the Riemann zeta function. For real x≥2 and integers 1≤m≤x define C_x(m)=Σ_{1≤n≤x−m}μ²(n)μ²(n+m). For real 1≤z≤y with Z=f(z)≤Y=f(y)≤x, define V_f(x;z,y)=Σ_{z<k≤y}f'(k)Σ_{l=1}^{f(k)}E(x;f(k),l)², T_f(z,y)=Σ_{z<k≤y}f'(k)Σ_{l=1}^{f(k)}g(f(k),l)², and S_f(x;z,y)=Σ_{z<k≤y}f'(k)Σ_{1≤h≤x/f(k)}C_x(hf(k)); all sums over k and h are over positive integers. For every ε>0 there is C(f,ε)>0 such that, uniformly throughout these ranges, |V_f(x;z,y)−[cx(Y−Z)+2S_f(x;z,y)−x²T_f(z,y)]|≤C(f,ε)[x^(3/2+ε)+xY^(1−1/d)]. In addition, uniformly for x≥2 and real z≥1 with f(z)≤x, 0≤V_f(x,z)≤C(f,ε)x^(1+ε)f(z)^(2−1/d).
cites: R. C. Vaughan, A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions (2005), Lemmas 2.2(ii), 2.3 and 2.4, specialized to k=2; https://doi.org/10.1112/S0024611505015352.

J. Brüdern, A. Granville, A. Perelli, R. C. Vaughan and T. D. Wooley, On the exponential sum over k-free numbers (1998), Lemma 2.2, specialized to k=2 and 1≤Q≤x; https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/on-the-exponential-sum-over-k-free-numbers/.
risk: The initial-modulus bound must use positivity before multiplying the full-modulus variance bound by the maximum polynomial weight. The mixed term requires divisibility counts, rather than a pointwise progression error multiplied by every residue class.
